articles.title: Conor McGregor to undergo surgery on knee injury which ended return fight against Max Holloway at UFC 329 but hopes to fight again
articles.summary: Conor McGregor outlined a plan for surgery, rehabilitation and another fight following a knee injury in his UFC 329 fight with Max Holloway which lasted just 69 seconds
articles.body:
The ​former two-weight world champion suffered the injury in the opening moments of his ​fight with Holloway on Sunday in Las Vegas when he landed awkwardly after attempting a jump ​kick.

McGregor tried to fight on for a few seconds but looked towards the referee to signal ​he could not continue.

"All things work ⁠out for my good! All ⁠things are possible for me because I am a believer!" McGregor wrote ‌on Instagram. "Surgery. Prehab. Return to martial arts practice. Go again. Final fight of the contract. Please God!"

Speaking after the fight, UFC president Dana White said: "Five years off in this sport is rough.

"We're assuming a blown ACL. That's what I assumed when I saw it and that's what the doctors think too."

Asked if there may have been an existing injury, White said there were no signs of it at last Friday's ceremonial weigh-in. White added that, with the millions of social-media views of McGregor rushing Holloway at the weigh-in, someone would have noticed if anyone was injured.

On Sunday, McGregor's manager, John Kavanagh, said his client did not have a previous knee injury.

"That opening jump switch kick was drilled daily for months, multiple times in warm-up. Never an issue," Kavanagh wrote on Facebook.

"Knee went when he [threw] the very first kick. Doesn't get any worse than this."

Following the fight, McGregor also said he had no previous injury. "I was throwing kicks, planted and jumping, all throughout camp as well as backstage before the fight," McGregor said on X.

"I had no injury/injuries going into the fight."

Injuries ‌and issues away from the sport have derailed the 37-year-old Irishman's career.

After breaking his leg against Dustin Poirier five years ago, McGregor was slated to meet Michael ⁠Chandler in June 2024 but that ​was cancelled after McGregor suffered a broken ​toe in training.

Later that year a jury ​in an Irish civil court found him liable ⁠for the assault of Nikita Hand, who had accused McGregor of rape, in 2018.

In October 2025, he accepted an 18-month ban for "whereabouts failures" ⁠after he missed three attempts ​by Combat Sports Anti-Doping to collect biological samples ​from him in 2024. The ban was backdated and expired in March.

articles.title: ONE Championship: Stephen Irvine eyes flyweight gold ahead of Suablack Tor Pran49 showdown at ONE Fight Night 45
articles.summary: Stephen Irvine seeks flyweight gold ahead of Suablack showdown in the co-main event of ONE Fight Night 45; the Scot holds a 30-4 record including seven wins but standing opposite him is one of Thailand's most experienced Muay Thai fighters
articles.body:
'El Matador' believes victory over Suablack can provide the perfect launchpad for a charge towards the ONE Championship flyweight Muay Thai world title.

The Scot faces the dangerous Thai in the co-main event of ONE Fight Night 45, in the early hours of Saturday morning from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium.

It marks another major milestone in Irvine's rapid rise after earning a £75,000 contract and a place on ONE Championship's global roster with a spectacular first-round head-kick knockout of Rambong Sor Therapat at ONE Friday Fights 128 in October 2025.

Now holding a 30-4 record including seven wins in ONE Championship, Irvine, who has competed exclusively in the strawweight ranks, begins the next chapter of his career by moving up to the promotion's flyweight Muay Thai division for the first time.

"It's good to be in the co-main event for my first ever fight on Fight Night," Irvine said. "It's a big compliment for me to be in the co-main event for my first appearance."

Standing opposite him is one of Thailand's most experienced Muay Thai fighters.

Suablack, who has become a viral sensation due to his extraordinarily muscular legs, earned his own place on ONE Championship's global roster after six consecutive victories on the ONE Friday Fights series. Now, four months following a loss in kickboxing, he returns to his Muay Thai roots.

Despite acknowledging that Suablack is likely to be the naturally bigger man, Irvine believes the move to flyweight will ultimately work in his favour.

"I've fought a lot of southpaws, so it's very similar to my other fights. Every fight is different, but I'm prepared for everything that he's got," he said.

"I think my skill set is better than his. It's a new weight for me, which is going to play into my hands.

"I know he's coming down [from bantamweight], so he'll be a bit bigger, but I'm going to have the speed advantage. I've studied Suablack a lot, and I'm confident that I can beat anything he has."

Suablack has promised to bring constant pressure when they meet on his home turf inside Lumpinee Stadium. But Irvine believes that approach will play directly into his own hands.

"I don't think it's a great idea for him," Irvine said.

"I've heard that's his plan, but I don't think that's going to be his best move. I wish him good luck with the game plan he has prepared. I don't think he'll be able to handle me. Let's wait and see how it goes."

Victory would establish Irvine as a genuine contender in one of ONE Championship's deepest Muay Thai divisions, although the 26-year-old accepts a world title opportunity will have to be earned.

"My goal is to be the champion," he said. "I'll do what it takes to get there. Every fight is a step in that direction.

"I know it's not there right now. I'll need to win a few fights, but I'll do what it takes. It might take some time, but that's okay."

His immediate prediction for Saturday's contest, however, was considerably more direct.

"I'm going to knock him out," Irvine said. "I'll get the kill. I'll get the bonus. That's what I'm expecting."

articles.title: ONE Championship: Stephen Irvine suffers brutal knockout by Suablack Tor Pran49 in showdown at ONE Fight Night 45
articles.summary: Stephen Irvine's quest for flyweight gold in the co-main event of ONE Fight Night 45 ended in defeat after a devasting elbow in the second round; the Scot now holds a 30-5 record after his defeat by one of Thailand's most experienced Muay Thai fighters
articles.body:
The Glasgow fighter was finished by a perfectly-timed elbow in the second round which earned his opponent the victory and the $50,000 performance bonus.

'El Matador', as he is known, was competing at a new weight class after stepping up from straweight and had been hoping to get a win over the 85-fight veteran to help propel a charge towards the ONE Championship flyweight Muay Thai world title.

And Irvine started well at Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium, evading Suablack's early boxing combinations before firing back with a crisp right hand that sent the Thai to the mat for an eight-count in the waning seconds of the opening round. For a moment, it looked like Irvine's pre-fight prediction of a knockout and a bonus might actually materialise.

It did, in fact, but sadly for him, it was the Thai southpaw who got it.

Irvine continued to apply pressure in the second round, walking his Thai rival down with punches, the occasional kick, and a few heavy elbows.

It all changed, though, nearly a minute into the frame when Suablack exploded forward with a left cross that knocked down the Scot and shifted the momentum.

Irvine answered the referee's eight-count and appeared completely level-headed, but the reprieve wouldn't last long.

The Scot moved forward in search of a knee strike, but Suablack retaliated with a body kick, another left cross, and then lunged forward with a powerful elbow that smashed Irvine's face with sickening precision and immediately crumbled him to the canvas.

Once again, the referee administered an eight-count, but when the Glasgow striker stumbled and failed to rise, the match was waved off.

For Irvine, fresh off earning a lucrative contract and a place on ONE Championship's global roster just nine months earlier, this was a harsh introduction to the flyweight division's elite. The move up in weight, which he'd convinced himself would play to his strengths, instead highlighted how much work remains before he can challenge for world title gold.

Suablack improved to 63-23 and announced himself as a genuine force in the flyweight Muay Thai division whereas Irvine will need to bounce back from a sobering defeat.

articles.title: Du Plessis makes winning return to UFC with dominant decision over Usman
articles.summary: South African fighter held the middleweight belt ⁠from January 2024 until August 2025 when he lost to Chimaev.
articles.body:
Dricus Du Plessis ‌has leaned on his South African roots in his first fight in nearly a year ⁠to secure ⁠a victory by unanimous decision over Nigeria’s Kamaru Usman in the middleweight main event of UFC Fight Night in Oklahoma City.

The judges on Saturday ⁠scored the bout 50-45, 49-46, 49-46 in favour of Du Plessis (24-3 MMA), who won his first nine UFC bouts and held the middleweight belt ⁠from January 2024 until mid-August last year.

“I had to get up,” the 32-year-old said. “There’s so many South African kids that look ‌up to me.

“It’s bigger than me. I can’t go lie down.”

In a fight contested upright with no successful takedowns or submission attempts, Du Plessis didn’t appear rusty whatsoever, finishing with a convincing 139-99 edge in total strikes and landing 136 significant strikes to Usman’s 92.

Usman (21-5) was the UFC welterweight champion from March 2019 to November 2021. ⁠However, the Nigerian, 39, has lost four of ⁠his last five fights and couldn’t add a second straight win in his first fight in 13 months this weekend.

articles.title: Conor McGregor calls for third UFC fight against Max Holloway in 2027
articles.summary: Star fighter wants another chance to take on Holloway after he sustained a knee injury at UFC 329 on July 11.
articles.body:
Conor McGregor has laid out ‌a long-term plan, seeking a ⁠rematch of ⁠his recent loss to Max Holloway in what would be the final bout of his Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) deal.

In ⁠an Instagram post that references the UFC’s International Fight Week next July, McGregor wrote on Monday, “What was to be ⁠a generational beating is now to be reset. IFW 2027. The Last Dance.”

Should McGregor oppose Holloway again, it would be the pair’s third matchup.

In a welterweight fight at UFC ‌329 in Las Vegas, Nevada, on July 11, Holloway (28-9) won by technical knockout in just 69 seconds after McGregor (22-7) hurt his right knee on an early kick.

The two fighters also squared off in August 2013, when McGregor won by unanimous decision.

McGregor, 38, is ⁠due to have his torn anterior ⁠cruciate ligament surgically repaired, which likely explains the long wait for the rematch.

Even though the Irish fighter recently posted an Instagram video showing him going through leg ⁠exercises, UFC president Dana White said on Sunday of McGregor, “Conor McGregor’s out for ⁠a year.”

The July 11 contest was ⁠McGregor’s first action in the Octagon in five years, since a technical knockout loss to Dustin Poirier at UFC 264 in Las Vegas. McGregor ‌has lost each of his past three bouts and four of the past five.

Holloway, a 34-year-old Honolulu native, ‌dropped ‌a unanimous decision to Charles Oliveira at UFC 326 in March in Las Vegas before bouncing back to defeat McGregor.

articles.title: Allan Nascimento: UFC fighter dies aged 34 after suffering apparent heart attack in his sleep
articles.summary: Allan Nascimento, the Brazilian flyweight, was found unresponsive on Monday; UFC pays tribute to "our beloved fighter and exemplary flyweight"
articles.body:
The Brazilian flyweight was found unresponsive on Monday after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep.

A UFC statement said: "This morning, Monday, August 3, our beloved fighter and exemplary flyweight Allan Nascimento was found unresponsive after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep.

"Despite the efforts of the responding medical team, he was pronounced deceased at the scene.

"Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Allan's family, friends, team-mates, and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time."

Nascimento, who had won 22 of his 29 bouts, last fought in June, when he lost to Mitch Raposo in Las Vegas on a split decision.

articles.title: Nascimento: UFC fighter dead at 34 after apparent heart attack
articles.summary: The Brazilian fighter died in his sleep after a suspected heart attack, the UFC said.
articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) fighter Allan Nascimento has died at the age of 34 after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep.

The mixed martial art (MMA) body posted the news about the Brazilian’s passing late Monday on their website.

“This morning, Monday, August 3rd, our beloved fighter and exemplary flyweight, Allan Nascimento, was found unresponsive after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep,” the UFC statement read.

articles.title: UFC 331: Van-Pantoja rematch, Tsarukyan returns and full fight card
articles.summary: Van and Pantoja to fight for flyweight title, while Tsarukyan faces the dangerous Mauricio Ruffy at lightweight.
articles.body:
Joshua Van and Alexandre Pantoja will headline UFC 331 in September in a flyweight title rematch on September 19 in Los Angeles, officials announced on Thursday.

Van won the title in their first bout with a first-round TKO in December that was blighted by an early injury to the defending champion Pantoja.

Meanwhile, lightweights Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy will fight in the co-main event.

Here’s everything you need to know about this card.

Van-Pantoja rematch: What happened in the first fight?

The co-main event fight at UFC 323 in Las Vegas lasted just 26 seconds as then-champion Pantoja (30-6) dislocated his elbow when he fell to the mat after Van (17-2) caught a kick and was unable to continue.

Van, aged just 24, became one of the youngest champions in the promotion’s history and ended Pantoja’s eight-fight win streak – including four defences of his title.

While Pantoja has been in rehabilitation since the loss, Van defended his title at UFC 328 when he knocked out Tatsuro Taira in the fifth round. Van is now on a seven-fight win streak.

Pantoja’s freak injury and the nature of the loss meant a rematch with Van was inevitable.

Tsarukyan: one of UFC’s biggest stars returns to the Octagon

While Tsarukyan (23-3) has been wrestling in the Real American Freestyle promotion recently, he last fought in the Octagon in November 2022 at Qatar UFC, when he beat Dan Hooker in the second round with an arm-triangle choke submission.

Tsarukyan is eager to work his way back to a title shot against Russia’s Islam Makhachev after the Armenian was forced to pull out of their fight in January 2025 with an injury.

But he faces a dangerous rising star in Ruffy (14-2), who most recently knocked out Michael Chandler in the first round of their bout at the UFC Freedom 250 event in June.

UFC 331 is set to take place on Saturday, September 19, 2026, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California, United States.

Early prelims begin about 5pm ET (21:00 GMT), prelims at 7pm ET (23:00 GMT), and the main card starts at 9pm ET (01:00 GMT on Sunday).

UFC 331 is broadcast live on Paramount+ in the US, TNT Sports in the United Kingdom, Foxtel/Kayo in Australia, Sportsnet+ in Canada, and on UFC Fight Pass worldwide.

What is the winner prediction for the main event?

Pantoja opens as a slight -120 favourite to win the fight according to DraftKings, with Van listed as a +100 underdog.

articles.title: Dana White: 'I know where the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua venue is - I did the deal!'
articles.summary: As speculation swirls around the date and venue for the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua showdown, Dana White reveals he knows where it will be; watch Zuffa Boxing 10, headlined by the Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha world title fight, live on Sky Sports on Saturday
articles.body:
White, who founded the UFC and new promotion Zuffa Boxing, is a major figure in combat sports. He revealed he knows where Fury vs Joshua will take place.

"We're the ones that have done all the deals for this fight. I did the deal for the venue, that's why I know where the venue is. I did the deal. We at TKO [the company which owns UFC, WWE and Zuffa Boxing] did the deal for television and we did everything," White told Sky Sports .

There has been much speculation that Fury vs Joshua could take place in the United States rather than Britain, with Eddie Hearn, Joshua's promoter, claiming: "I really feel strongly that this is something that should happen in the UK and we'll do all we can."

White told Sky Sports : "At the end of the day, here's the truth, you're going to go where the money is."

Heavyweight rivals Joshua and Fury have been circling one another for almost a decade and yet a fight between the pair has never come to fruition.

"It's just been such a [mess]. It's unbelievable what a [mess] this thing has been," White said.

"It goes to show why boxing has been so [messed] up for so long. Look at this. It's definitely not about the money. The Saudis are paying for this fight. So they're making [a lot] of money. And what I've noticed is in the boxing business since I've been in it for a very short period of time, six months, the promoters' egos are actually more important than the fights themselves and giving the fight fans the fights they want to see.

"It's all about ego with the promoters. It's fascinating. These guys are all really weak, some of the weakest people I've ever encountered in the fight game. It's fascinating."

Sky Sports has contacted Matchroom and Queensberry, the promoters of Joshua and Fury, for comment.

Fury was a guest at White's UFC event at the White House and the promoter has known both fighters from before he launched his own boxing business.

"I've talked about Anthony Joshua after he beat (Wladimir) Klitschko and I was like that's what boxing needs, good looking, charismatic, good speaking heavyweight champion. So I've always really liked Anthony Joshua," White said.

"There was a point in time where Tyson was stagnant and trying to get fights so he started talking [trash] about UFC fighters, trying to get a payday one way or another and that was around the time that I met him and I've always liked him.

"Tough as hell, when he was dropped by (Deontay) Wilder [and] he gets right back up like a zombie and finishes the fight. He's a fun guy to watch. He's one of the best ever."

articles.title: Joe Ward rescues career with valiant Artjom Kasparian win as Stevie McKenna and Sam Hickey take stunning one-punch finishes
articles.summary: Joe Ward wins ferocious Artjom Kasparian battle; Sam Hickey and Stevie McKenna take stunning one-punch finishes; Watch Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha and Callum Walsh vs Tyler Denny live on Sky Sports Action or Sky Sports Main Event
articles.body:
Ward was a true amateur boxing sensation. At 17, all the way back in 2011, he became Ireland's youngest ever senior European gold medallist.

Though he became an Olympian, misfortune dogged his amateur career, and his pro start was even worse. He dislocated his knee and lost his professional debut.

This fight at the 3Arena in Dublin was his first since 2024 and his ticket back to the big-time

Ward did begin like he'd never been away. He peppered Kasparian with sharp southpaw punching, popping shots into the body and the head. The Manchester-based hitter even picked up a nick by his right eye.

Kasparian stayed in front of his opponent though and in the third round consecutive right hooks to the jaw tested out Ward's chin and the visitor would then test the home hero to his limit.

Kasparian refused to take a backwards step. Ward's arms began to look tired and he leaned on in a clinch.

Kasparian's solution was to keep on throwing and keep hitting out with heavy shots.

The visitor got himself onto the front foot at the start of the fourth round, landing a double jab and snagging Ward as he stepped in.

Ward rapidly tired, punching with just his arms, his feet rooted to the spot, his head available to be hit. That is not the place to be against a big puncher like Kasparian.

Kasparian kept up a strong assault through the middle rounds of the fight. He was, at times, pummelling Ward and it looked like the Irishman was on the brink of disaster.

But, as well as talent, Ward has heart. He pulled it back, and brought in strong backhands to repel Kasparian in the seventh round.

Ward pounced on the opportunity, getting a second wind. He bounced a one-two off Kasparian's head in the eighth round and started to dictate the action.

Under pressure Kasparian almost fell through the ropes and the crowd wildly cheered for Ward.

In the ninth round, Ward screwed his right in and slammed his left down again. Kasparian, though, hacked at him with left hooks.

Ward popped in a clean, accurate left cross and Kasparian staggered back a step. He harried Kasparian with a sustained combination before the round was up.

Kasparian banged in a one-two but Ward, marked under his right eye, managed to trade with gusto. Kasparian tried to reel away, but Ward kept on throwing, catching him.

Fiercely determined Kasparian slugged back, but Ward answered in kind and raised both arms in the air at the final bell.

Stevie McKenna , with older brother Aaron starring in the main event, got a memorable evening for his family off to a sensational start.

He stormed out to meet Owen O'Neill, loomed over his opponent, and slung out heavy punches. O'Neill hopped backwards, hoping to ride out the storm. But McKenna did not relent. He stayed on his prey, whacking him with a massive left hook and continuing to strafe him with wide-arm punches.

O'Neill was left with little option but to tuck up beneath the onslaught. That though was just an invitation for trouble. A one-two from McKenna lanced down and a right cross sent O'Neill flying off his feet, crashing down on the canvas. He had to be stopped there and then in the first round.

Slick Scottish middleweight prospect Sam Hickey scored a second consecutive victory with a monstrous one-punch finish.

Brad Axe was a competitive opponent, digging in and firing back when Hickey clipped him.

In the third round Hickey stepped in and short right to the side of the head dropped Axe to a knee. The bell though rang to save him.

But Axe kept himself in the fight and caught Hickey in return. Regularly though Hickey finished rounds strongly, driving Axe into the ropes only for the bell to call him off.

Hickey though finished matters at the start of the seven round, Axe bounced in and a booming right greeted him, spinning him round as he flopped down to the canvas. The towel immediately came in as Axe suffered a heavy stoppage.

Romania's Daniel Buciuc managed to get through six rounds with Louis Greene , though was in severe trouble in the closing seconds of the bout.

After a quiet first round, Greene closed down Buciuc's space, hammering his body with hooks. He brought hard, chopping shots through the middle jolting the Romanian.

Buciuc soon was trying to move off but he couldn't keep himself clear. Greene took him to the ropes and Buciuc had to endure salvoes of punchers, hefty uppercuts jolting him.

He attempted to tie up Greene but that left him open to the Briton's overarm right.

Buciuc was hanging on as Greene shook him up in the final half-minute of the contest. With his legs loosening, Buciuc still kept himself upright and got through to the final bell, Greene winning 59-55.

Connor Coyle took a unanimous points decision win after a bruising 10 rounds with the USA's Mark Beuke. The man from Derry put himself in the ascendancy in the early going of the bout, teeing up some solid right hands that blasted straight into Coyle.

But the American took his power and a cut opened by Coyle's right eye to complicate his evening's efforts.

Beuke stood his ground and kept Coyle honest with heavy hooks that he managed to land with either hand. But his successes came as single blows. Coyle worked better combinations and made sure he finished their exchanges with accurate punching.

Coyle finished the bout bleeding from the nose, but reeling off straight punches to push Beuke back, winning 98-92, 98-93 and 97-93.

Patrick O'Connor , a top American cruiserweight prospect with Irish roots, made short work of Spain's Juan Manuel Moriel.

Measured with his jab, O'Connor quickly took control. He lashed a right over and began to work the body as he ramped up his attack. The American finished a blazing combination of hooks to Moriel's trunk with a left hook to the head.

With O'Connor about to move through the gears, the bout was stopped after the first round, Moriel citing a shoulder injury as he stayed on his stool.

The American remains unbeaten in four pro fights, all of those wins coming inside the distance.

articles.title: Callum Walsh comes through cuts and knockdown to drop Denny and take battling decision victory in Dublin contest
articles.summary: Callum Walsh beats Tyler Denny by unanimous decision at the 3Arena in Dublin; Both had knockdowns scored against them; Watch Aaron McKenna fight Etinosa Oliha for the middleweight world title live on Sky Sports Action or Sky Sports Main Event
articles.body:
Denny, a former European champion, is a tough veteran and proved a test for the Irish middleweight at Dublin's 3Arena.

Walsh prevailed on points, winning 98-91 twice and 96-90.

The bout didn't progress without its pitfalls as Denny gave him hard rounds.

The first round suddenly went south for Walsh. Awkwardly positioned in front of Denny, he found himself bending low. Denny attacked and Walsh took a shot before slipping to a knee. The referee ruled that a knockdown.

Walsh found the perfect riposte in the second round. As Denny came after him, Walsh launched a lovely arching left cross to the point of the Englishman's chin, dropping him heavily to the canvas.

Denny, brave as ever, rose and fought on. But Walsh popped up from beneath an attack to land a fine right hook and he finished the round slugging Denny into the ropes.

The Briton shook off the effects of that round and advanced. By the end of the fourth round, Walsh was backing up, letting his southpaw opponent come on but picking out accurate punches to catch Denny.

Walsh maintained his control, moving, hitting and letting Denny work to try to pin him down.

The Briton kept scrapping forward and managed to land solidly in the sixth round.

Denny trudged on swinging wildly, but Walsh manoeuvred well. The Irishman caught Denny to the head with a left-right combination. Denny felt those shots but remained doggedly determined. He cleaved away with uppercuts in close.

The referee took a point off Walsh for holding, before evening up it by taking a point off Denny for hitting behind the head.

Walsh exploded forward with a savage sequence of punches to the head, leaving Denny stranded, standing still on the end of them.

But Walsh emerged from a clash with a cut over his left eye. It bled badly at once. Denny was leaning into him in scrappy collisions and Walsh looked frustrated after picking an additional nick on his cheek.

In the 10th round Walsh landed a great lead right uppercut. Denny got after him with hooks, catching the Irishman with his southpaw left and right.

Another hard left from Walsh though snagged Denny. He couldn't put the Englishman down a second time but made sure he finished the fight in the ascendancy.

Walsh told Sky Sports : "It was a lot harder than I thought. In the second round we clashed heads. I think he broke my orbital bone. It was crunching the whole time.

"It was very tough. I'm very critical of myself. I should have been a lot better. I wish I could have been better.

"He's tough, awkward and tricky, but we'll go again."

articles.title: Aaron McKenna wins dream homecoming bout against Etinosa Oliha to become IBF middleweight world champion in Dublin
articles.summary: Ireland's Aaron McKenna becomes a new middleweight world champion on an emotional night at the 3Arena in Dublin; McKenna seized a unanimous decision victory over Etinosa Oliha, winning  118-110, 117-111 and 116-112 on the scorecards in the headline bout on Zuffa Boxing 10
articles.body:
For McKenna this fight in Dublin was a dream homecoming. The Irish middleweight had pursued his career across America, sparring in some of the world's best gyms and amassing an undefeated pro record.

This contest, for the vacant IBF middleweight title, was his first world title fight and his first professional contest in Ireland.

With brother Stevie taking a spectacular knockout earlier, McKenna made a memorable entrance, wildly cheered into the ring by the 3Arena crowd, so loudly that the floor was almost rumbling.

But he didn't let emotions carry him away at the start of the fight. He edged forward onto the front foot, feinting. He timed a left hook as Oliha, unbeaten himself coming in, stepped to him.

McKenna let his jab flicker out. His hands were quick, his right streaked in and McKenna used his left hook to let a cross blast through.

But the Italian wrested the second round his way, thumping through right hooks, punches McKenna felt, to show that he too could launch meaningful attacks.

McKenna ground forward, stifling his own long-range work but bodily forcing Oliha back.

When he did strike his opponent with a reaching right, the crowd roared and as the fight progressed into its second half McKenna did move more on his toes, darting back to scrape his left hook into the side of Oliha's head.

The Italian looked to rip hooks into him but McKenna marshalled him to the ropes and slugged Oliha with a left hook.

McKenna imposed himself again in the ninth round but Oliha, a solid operator, showed little sign of wilting.

In the 10th round McKenna circled out and reeled off double jabs. As they grappled in a clinch though, Oliha unleashed a flurry that caught the Irishman.

McKenna briefly put space between them with a cross to the chin. He scored to the body with thudding right hooks too.

Oliha charged from his corner with a long one-two to start the 11th round. With flashier work, McKenna landed a left uppercut off his jab. Oliha though hacked back at him with a right hook up close.

McKenna continued to punch in greater volume. A clash saw him cut on the forehead just before the end of the 11th. He trusted in a hefty right hook as a response.

He didn't want or need to take risks in the last round. He moved sharply, striking an increasingly desperate Oliha with jabs and the crowd all around him stood up cheering, clapping and chanting his name.

McKenna worked an uppercut, Oliha drove in a right but even when McKenna took shots he didn't let them shake him as he closed out a unanimous decision.

When that final bell chimed, McKenna rushed to the corner post and jumped up onto the ropes to celebrate.

As soon as the words "from Monaghan" were declared by the ring announcer, confirming McKenna a 118-110, 117-111 and 116-112 victor, the arena burst into deafening cheers once again.

"A new world champion. I've been saying it for years. A big thank you to Zuffa Boxing for giving me this platform and bringing a fight back to Ireland for me," McKenna beamed afterwards.

"I've been a professional for nine years and never got the chance to fight in Ireland. Why? Just look at these beautiful fans.

"I never lost discipline in training. There were times when I wondered whether I'd ever get the chance.

"My dad [their trainer] sacrificed his whole life for me and my brother, dedicating everything to helping us chase our dreams.

articles.title: Aaron McKenna vows middleweight domination as heir to Gennadiy Golovkin and Canelo Alvarez after world title win
articles.summary: Aaron McKenna beat Etinosa Oliha in Dublin on Saturday to become the new IBF middleweight world champion; the Irishman is determined to clean up "this mess of a division"; McKenna declared: "I think I'm going to be the man to take it over"
articles.body:
He secured the IBF middleweight title with a victory over Etinosa Oliha on memorable night at the 3Arena in Dublin.

Now he wants to take on the mantle of Canelo Alvarez and Gennadiy Golovkin by dominating the middleweight division.

He is targeting other champions. Denzel Bentley holds the WBO title, Carlos Adames the WBC and Erislandy Lara the WBA. McKenna is calling for all the top 160-pounders to fight one another.

"It doesn't matter [who's next], whoever wants it. I'm easy to find now, I have a belt. There's no hiding any more. I want to collect every single belt in boxing. I'm the best middleweight and super-middleweight in the world. I don't mind jumping up," he told Sky Sports .

"I've been thinking about this moment since I was six years old. It just goes to show, don't give up, always stay true to yourself. You can do anything."

His ambitions extend far. "The middleweight division's there to be took over. It's been dying for years since GGG (Golovkin) and Canelo left it. I said it again, a year ago, I think I'm going to be the man to take it over," McKenna declared at his post-fight press conference.

"No one really believed me. Until you put in performances like that and then they start listening. In life you've got to prove yourself sometimes. Tonight I've done that. I just hope one of the other world champions will take on the fight so we can clean up this mess of a division."

He promises he will not shy away from any challenge.

"Anyone. I've said it before and I'll say it again I will literally fight anyone out there. I just want to unify, whatever it takes, prove I'm the best in the world. That's the sport of boxing. You look back in the day, the 80s and 90s, they all fought each other," McKenna said.

"And this is exactly why Zuffa Boxing's going to be the future. It's already taking over. Everybody's fighting each other, there's no more hiding."

For the time being, he can enjoy his accomplishment.

"Twenty-one years in the making," he concluded. "I don't know how long this is going to take for this to seep in that this has finally happened that I've become world champion. I've been dreaming of this.

"For it to happen now, honestly it's literally unbelievable. I can't describe it."

articles.title: Dina Thorslund ends Cherneka Johnson's undisputed run to become world champion again after return following miscarriage
articles.summary: Dina Thorslund snatches WBC, WBO, WBA and IBF titles from Cherneka Johnson, winning every round in a unanimous decision in the main event of MVPW-5 in Orlando, Florida; it was an emotional triumph for Thorslund, who returned to the ring following a miscarriage
articles.body:
Just over a year after vacating her WBC and WBO bantamweight titles because she was pregnant, the undefeated Thorslund fought aggressively from the start to snatch the WBC, WBO, WBA and IBF titles from Johnson, winning every round in a unanimous decision in the main event of MVPW-5 in Orlando, Florida.

Thorslund (25-0, nine KOs) vacated her titles in June 2025, and a month later she announced on social media that she had suffered a miscarriage.

She returned to the ring in January and defeated Almudena Alvarez to capture the vacant WBC interim featherweight title. Then Thorslund, who is 32 years old and from Denmark, dropped back to bantamweight to fight for the undisputed championship.

The lead-up to Saturday's fight brought more emotional turmoil for Thorslund, whose training partner, Raven Chapman, underwent emergency brain surgery last month after she collapsed during a sparring session in Denmark.

"This has been such an emotional journey for me the last year," Thorslund said, fighting back tears.

"I'm going to take this [title belt] straight back to Raven and say thank you."

Thorslund was in control for the whole fight. Her aggressive combinations put Johnson on the defensive, especially early, and through three rounds, Thorslund had landed 37 punches to Johnson's 14. In the end, Thorslund's non-stop attack of power punches built a 103-62 edge. All three judges scored it 100-90.

Johnson (19-3, eight KOs), who became undisputed champion by knocking out Shurretta Metcalf in July 2025, was unable to utilise her power against Thorslund. Practically every time she connected, Thorslund would respond by landing three or four shots in return.

articles.title: Conor Benn vows to wreak havoc against Ryan Garcia to capture WBC welterweight title
articles.summary: Conor Benn has vowed to stop Ryan Garcia and "cause havoc" when they meet for the WBC welterweight title in Las Vegas on September 12; Benn says Garcia's mind games are "just noise" as he targets the belt once held by his father Nigel
articles.body:
Benn will contest his first-career world title fight against WBC welterweight champion Garcia on September 12 in Las Vegas.

Garcia, one of the most high-profile fighters in the sport, has engaged in a war of words with Benn, but the Brit is focused on emphatically silencing the American once and for all.

"It's all just noise," Benn told Sky Sports . "It doesn't really concern me, doesn't bother me. I'm just coming there to take his title off him.

"I plan on going in there and getting a stoppage, for sure. I'm just going to go in there and do what I do, which is plant one on his chin and try and put him to sleep.

"I prepare diligently hard and always put the work in. I've taken it with both hands and I'm coming in there to cause havoc."

Benn enters the fight off the back of beating Regis Prograis on the undercard of Tyson Fury's comeback fight against Arslanbek Makhmudov in April.

It was at the same venue, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, which staged Benn's epic two-fight rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr.

Having avenged his first professional defeat at the hands of Eubank Jr in their November 2025 rematch, Benn has set his sights on emulating his father Nigel by winning the WBC belt he held and defended in 11 fights between 1992 and 1995.

"For me to get a world title shot, the prestigious WBC world title, the belt my dad won, it's a blessing," he added.

"That's not my driving factor. My driving factor is to do it for myself. It's for me to prove that I'm one of the best in the world."

Garcia represents a marked step up in the quality of opposition Benn has faced previously, but he is relishing his underdog status.

"I like being the underdog," he said. "I think I perform at my best.

"I think every single one of my fights has led me to this moment. All the pressure I've had early on in my career has prepared me for nights like those at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

"It's prepared me for the noise and the drama and the chaos. So come September 12, it's nothing new, nothing different."

articles.title: Caroline Dubois: Britain's lightweight world champion has 'ingredients' to succeed Katie Taylor as face of boxing, says Nakisa Bidarian
articles.summary: Caroline Dubois will take on Amelia Moore in Birmingham on August 29; the event will be headlined by Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron, who will compete for the unified welterweight world championship; watch MVPW-06 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Ireland's undisputed super-lightweight world champion Taylor, who turned 40 in July, is set to fight professionally for the final time in an undisputed world super-lightweight title fight against Flora Pili in Dublin on September 5.

A week earlier, lightweight world champion Dubois will seek to maintain her unbeaten record when she defends her WBC and WBO straps against American Amelia Moore, live on Sky Sports on the undercard of Chantelle Cameron's clash with Mikaela Mayer.

Bidarian told Sky Sports : "For me, the poster fighters of the sport have been Amanda Serrano and Katie Taylor, the two of them have been real trailblazers.

"It's sad to see that arc transition in September for Katie, I think Amanda probably has one more fight left after August 21.

"But women's boxing has never been stronger. It's a young sport, it became an Olympic sport in 2012 where Katie was the beneficiary, and she's created a storied career for herself.

"But we feel good about the future of this sport we feel like we have a roster of athletes. Caroline Dubois is one who I think has the ingredients of Katie Taylor, Amanda Serrano, Laila Ali, Christy Martin and Ronda Rousey all there.

"Of course, the sport's going to miss Katie, of course the ring is going to miss Amanda, but the sport is in a great place."

Salita says Shields is 'definitively No 1'

Undisputed heavyweight champion Claressa Shields is already "definitively" the No 1 fighter in women's boxing, according to her promoter Dmitry Salita.

Two-time Olympic gold medallist Shields has been an undisputed champion in the professional ranks in three weight classes, winning all 18 of her fights.

Asked about Shields' status in the sport amid Taylor's career coming to a close, Salita told Sky Sports earlier this year: "Katie Taylor is a historic figure in boxing, and I've said many times - personally and professionally - that I'm a fan of hers and what she has done for the sport.

"That said, Claressa Shields is definitively the No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter in women's boxing today.

"What separates Claressa is not just what she's accomplished in the ring which already stands on its own but the totality of her impact.

"There is something more to being a bona fide superstar than simply being elite in the ring. There's an "it" factor. The ability to headline, to sell out arenas, to create moments, to carry events regardless of the opponent - and Claressa has that. "She may be the first woman in the history of the sport consistently selling out major arenas regardless of opponent."

Shields is dropping down from heavyweight in an attempt to become middleweight world champion once more, with the 31-year-old taking on Australian Kaye Scott in Atlanta this weekend.

The fight could be a precursor for a possible blockbuster with Britain's own world champion Lauren Price, who currently holds three of the four welterweight belts.

Talks have previously taken place over Shields and Price meeting at the middleweight, and despite an impasse in negotiations, Salita remains optimistic the fight can happen.

"When Claressa went to Wales, we believed we had the framework of a deal in place, and we're still operating in that spirit," Salita told Sky Sports last month.

"I believe we're close. Claressa is moving down to 160 pounds because she wants to make this fight happen. She's already accomplished so much, but she's always looking for the biggest global fights.

"Lauren is an outstanding fighter and an Olympic gold medallist. This is one of the biggest fights that can be made in women's boxing, and we're confident it will happen.

"Claressa has always done her part to make the biggest fights possible, and this is no different. We're ready to continue the discussions."

articles.title: Jarrell Miller could receive world heavyweight title fight as Murat Gassiev is 'interested' in fighting the American
articles.summary: Jarrell Miller aims to challenge Murat Gassiev for WBA heavyweight belt; Miller could finally receive world title fight following cancelled clash against Anthony Joshua after American tested positive for banned substances in 2019; WBA champion Gassiev is 'interested' in fighting Miller
articles.body:
The WBA recently clarified that Miller is not a mandatory challenger for Gassiev, despite initially announcing this status, but the 38-year-old American still hopes to receive a world title fight against the Russian champion.

Miller confirmed to Sky Sports that a WBA title shot could be next after his points win over Cuban Lenier Pero in April and Gassiev has also revealed that he is open to the fight.

"Yes, if there is an offer regarding Jarrell Miller, we are of course interested," Gassiev told Sky Sports.

"Furthermore, if Moses Itauma decides to pursue the IBF route, Jarrell Miller will become an official contender for my WBA title, making the fight inevitable for me.

"We are also highly interested in a fight with [WBC champion] Agit Kabayel. If a concrete agreement is reached and this fight begins to materialise, I would gladly sign up for a unification bout.

"It all comes down to the specifics - the offer, the terms, the timing, and the venue. We are targeting fights that make sense both financially and for my career progression."

Moses Itauma is the current WBA No 1 contender, but the unbeaten Brit will fight Filip Hrgovic for the vacant IBF belt on August 19, which should mean that Miller, ranked at No 2 by the WBA, is next in line for Gassiev.

The controversial Brooklyn boxer, nicknamed 'Big Baby', defeated Kingsley Ibeh by split decision in a January fight that went viral after Miller's hairpiece was dislodged in the second round.

Miller could finally receive a shot at a world heavyweight title, more than seven years after his scheduled 2019 fight against Anthony Joshua for the WBA, IBF and WBO titles was cancelled after Miller tested positive for banned substances .

Gassiev was elevated to become the WBA world heavyweight champion after Oleksandr Usyk vacated his WBA, WBC and IBF belts in June.

The 32-year-old defended his WBA title with a sixth-round stoppage win over Peter Kadiru in Moscow last month and is now eager to acquire more world belts.

"It's not just about Kabayel. To put it simply, I want any unification bout available," Gassiev told Sky Sports.

"However, if defending my WBA title against a mandatory challenger becomes the immediate priority, that would be an excellent matchup for me and all boxing fans.

"In that scenario, we will gladly fulfil our mandatory obligations.

"That said, our ultimate goal remains a unification fight. The same applies to the winner of Dubois vs Wardley [for the WBO belt] or Itauma vs Hrgovic.

"We are genuinely interested in any available unification fights."

articles.title: Stevie McKenna is 'locked in' on all-Irish showdown with Callum Walsh after viral KO win, says manager Mike Borao
articles.summary: Stevie McKenna is targeting Irish rival Callum Walsh after knockout of Owen O'Neill went viral on social media; Walsh extended his unbeaten record with points win over Tyler Denny on same bill; McKenna's manager Mike Borao says Walsh fight can be in a major stadium in Ireland or New York
articles.body:
McKenna produced a spectacular knockout victory over Owen O'Neill that went viral on social media before his younger brother Aaron was crowned IBF middleweight champion in the main event of Zuffa Boxing 10 on Saturday.

On the same bill, Walsh preserved his unbeaten record with a hard-fought win over Tyler Denny and could now be heading for an explosive clash with Stevie McKenna.

"At the moment, Stevie is locked on one fight - Callum Walsh in a major stadium in Ireland or New York. It's all he talks about," his manager Borao told Sky Sports.

"The crowd's reaction after the fight, when Stevie asked if that's what they wanted to see next, made it clear this would be a major attraction.

"Stevie has even mentioned to me that he would be open to stepping up against [WBA world champion] Erislandy Lara next.

"We'll sit with our partners at Zuffa and decide what's next for Stevie. They've been outstanding. That relationship already delivered a world title for Aaron in short order, and I have no doubt a major opportunity will follow for Stevie."

McKenna has returned with first round knockout wins over O'Neill and Casey James Streeter in June since his first career loss on points to Lee Cutler in December 2024.

Borao, who secured an IBF world heavyweight title fight for Frank Sanchez, has also guided Teofimo Lopez to a WBA welterweight title fight against Rolly Romero later this month, and believes Stevie McKenna is next to land a major fight.

"Zuffa and Sky Sports have been incredible for Aaron and Stevie's careers," said Borao.

"It's remarkable how involved Dana White and Zuffa are in backing their athletes. Aaron and Stevie have never received this type of support.

"Stevie is must-see TV - his latest knockout proved it, but the best is yet to come!"

articles.title: Ruby White: Commonwealth Games silver medallist sends message to Sakshi Chaudhary after final defeat in Glasgow
articles.summary: Ruby White wants "revenge" on Sakshi Chaudhary after her defeat in the gold medal bout at the Commonwealth Games; White is targeting gold for Team GB at the 2028 Olympics
articles.body:
The 19-year-old was unbeaten in 71 fights heading into the final, but couldn't extend her incredible streak and take the gold as a 5-0 defeat to Indian Sakshi Chaudhary saw her secure a silver medal in the women's 51kg category in Glasgow.

White's boxing career, though, is just beginning - and as far as she is concerned, the story between her and Chaudhary is far from over.

"When I'm a little bit more experienced in the senior ranks, I want to get my revenge!

"I was a little bit underprepared for the fight. I had a lot of pressure on me, first multi-sport games, first senior tournament. So I know I can get in there and win - I've just got to change the game plan a little bit more."

Despite her defeat in the final, White prefers to reflect on the positive moments from a tournament she had dreamt of fighting at during childhood.

"I had four very good fights and lost out on the finals. But to reflect back on it, being 19 and to go to the Commonwealth Games after only being selected for GB a couple of months prior, and to come back with silver in my first major tournament, it's amazing.

"I was very upset in the ring after I lost, but I'm on a good path and everything's been amazing ever since.

"It's all experience as an amateur until you get to the Olympics - that when it really matters - but the Commonwealth Games was such an amazing start.

"From seven years old, I worked it out: I always dreamt of going to the 2026 Commonwealth Games and then the 2028 Olympics.

"I'm on the right track to be at such a big tournament. To come away with silver is an achievement, and I'm happy."

White's success has caught the attention of many notable names across British boxing, but the one that stuck out most to her was that of Nicola Adams. The two-time Olympic gold medalist is an idol of White's - and she is hoping to emulate her success for Team GB in 2028.

"Nicola Adams - she surprised me on the radio, and she told me that I'm amazing and I'm on the right track and to keep focused.

"[An olympic gold medal] would be absolutely amazing. I'm just really going to keep training and living life like an athlete. Hopefully I can get to LA [in 2028] and I can bring that gold medal home."

Dubois, who is also signed to MVP, had previously expressed her frustration after being unable to agree a world lightweight unification fight with Turhan, but those negotiations could get simpler now both fighters are aligned in Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian's promotional company.

Turhan, who is also undefeated in 14 fights, secured the IBF world lightweight title after a stunning stoppage of Beatriz Ferreira and has since retained her title in victories against Gabriella Tellez and Taylah Gentzen.

"Elif Nur Turhan is an undefeated world champion, a tremendous puncher, and now the first Turkish fighter to join the MVP roster," said MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian.

articles.title: Damar Thomas unfazed by Anthony Joshua comparisons as Commonwealth Games gold medallist chases 'own legacy' ahead of LA Olympics
articles.summary: Damar Thomas followed in the footsteps of Joe Joyce, Frazer Clarke and Delicious Orie at the Commonwealth Games but has since dismissed Anthony Joshua comparisons; the 21-year-old super-heavyweight is targeting success at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles
articles.body:
The boxer followed in the footsteps of Joe Joyce, Frazer Clarke and Delicious Orie when he beat India's Narender Berwal via unanimous decision to win gold in the super-heavyweight category.

Standing at 6ft 6in, Thomas has earned inevitable comparisons with Anthony Joshua and represents one of the great hopes for the future of British heavyweight boxing.

The 21-year-old, who is targeting success at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, is unfazed by such comparisons and insists he is focused on his own development.

"Yeah, it's a great feeling [to win gold]. I managed to add my name to the British heavyweights that won the Commonwealth [gold]," he said.

"Hopefully in LA I'll be able to add my name to those great heavyweights that managed to get Olympic gold.

"I'm just in my own race at the minute and taking it in my own strides. I'm not comparing myself to anyone. I'm doing everything at my own pace, which is great. What I want to do is create my own legacy, which is a good feeling."

Thomas demonstrated significant boxing IQ in his 5-0 victory over Berwal, marking his 11th consecutive win in a run that extends back to November.

"My main asset is my feet and my speed," Thomas said.

"That's what works for me with these heavyweights, because a lot of these heavyweights rely on one shot. I don't rely on that, so it's great."

While Thomas' main ambition for now is to remain amateur and win gold in LA, he has his sights set on becoming a professional after the games in 2028.

"First, I want to tick off that box with LA. I'm taking one tournament at a time," he added.

"It's a marathon, not a sprint. And I'm just taking everything at my own pace.

"The main goal is the Olympics. Until then, I'm thinking about Olympics and nothing else. But after the Olympics, I'll definitely turn professional."

articles.title: Craig Richards vs Radivoje Kalajdzic, Lee Cutler vs Louis Greene added to Johnny Fisher boxing bill at Copper Box Arena
articles.summary: Zuffa Boxing adds Craig Richards-Radivoje Kalajdzic and Lee Cutler-Louis Greene bouts to Copper Box Arena bill headlined by Johnny Fisher's latest heavyweight fight; watch it all live on Sky Sports on September 26
articles.body:
Richards vs Kalajdzic will serve as the chief support bout to the 10-round heavyweight main event featuring Fisher at Zuffa Boxing 11 on September 26, live on Sky Sports .

An opponent for 'The Romford Bull' will be announced in the coming days.

Richards (20-4-1, 13 KOs) is a world-ranked former British champion who fought Dmitry Bivol for the WBA light-heavyweight title in 2021. He won his two most recent fights in 2025, including a knockout win over Dan Azeez last December.

The fight will mark the first time hard-hitting, Serbian-born Kalajdzic (30-3, 22 KOs) has fought outside North America as a professional. The 35-year-old's last fight was a seventh-round knockout victory against Oleksandr Gvozdyk in February.

The Copper Box Arena bill will also feature a 10-round middleweight showdown between British boxers Cutler and Greene.

Cutler beat Stevie McKenna on points when they fought in December 2024, marking the only professional defeat for Ireland's KO king so far.

Cutler's last fight saw him stop Aaron Sutton in his hometown of Bournemouth in three rounds, while Greene - a former Commonwealth super-welterweight champion - earned a points decision win over Daniel Buciuc in Dublin last week.

Decorated British amateur Kayla Allen is also fighting as part of her professional debut after becoming the first female fighter to sign with Zuffa Boxing.

Alex MacMillan, Leon Hughes and Fred Pullen, who is also turning professional, are also on the London bill.

Richards: My story isn't written yet - the time is now

Craig "Spider" Richards speaking on Sky Sports News:

"It's a very exciting fight. Everyone knows Kalajdzic can punch, I can punch, we've both been two fighters who haven't shied away from competition.

"We've been in with everyone, we've mixed it, we both probably want to push on now towards that world title and I feel like it's a great opportunity.

"UK vs USA - that mix always goes down well! I'm up for it, I'm excited and I think this is now going to be the best version of me going into the new chapter and I get to go and display what I'm about.

"I feel like my story is not written yet and I feel like I need to write it now.

"The problem we had before is that a lot of opponents were turning [a fight with] me down, saying 'he's a hard fight, he's a long night in the office'.

"Zuffa doesn't allow you to do that, and that means I can get some activity. I can go out there and make a statement."

articles.title: Prichard Colon: Boxer dies aged 33 more than a decade after suffering severe brain injury
articles.summary: Prichard Colon suffered brain haemorrhage in fateful 2015 fight against Terrel Williams that left the Puerto Rican fighter in a coma for 221 days and in a vegetative state for the rest of his life
articles.body:
Colon, then aged 23, collapsed in his dressing room after his October 2015 fight against Terrel Williams in Virginia.

The Puerto Rican suffered a brain haemorrhage and was rushed to hospital, where he underwent emergency surgery that left him in a coma for 221 days.

Colon spent the rest of his life in a vegetative state, unable to walk and requiring 24-hour care.

"Good morning, my people. I'm sorry to inform you of the passing of my son Prichard from this earthly world," Colon's father, Richard, wrote on Facebook.

"He is now in a better world. I did everything I could to fulfil his desire and his dream of bringing him to Puerto Rico on holiday, as he wanted, but it couldn't happen.

"Thank you for so many years of love and prayers. Please keep us in your prayers as much as you can."

Colon, a former super welterweight, was undefeated in 16 fights as a professional before facing Williams.

He was disqualified after removing his gloves at the end of round nine before his condition deteriorated and he was rushed to hospital.

The World Boxing Organization posted a tribute to Colon on social media, saluting his warrior spirit until the end.

"The WBO family mourns the passing of Prichard Colón, whose courage, strength and fighting spirit transcended the ring," it wrote on X.

"His greatest fight became a testament to resilience and the unwavering love of his family."

articles.title: Claressa Shields vs Lauren Price is 'mega event' that 'belongs in United States' says the American's promoter Dmitriy Salita
articles.summary: Claressa Shields can reclaim the WBC and WBA middleweight belts when she faces Kaye Scott in Atlanta in the early hours of Sunday morning; Shields is then expected to fight Britain's Lauren Price and the American's star's promoter says the Welsh boxer should come to the USA for the fight
articles.body:
Shields can add another world title triumph to her long list of achievements when she fights Kaye Scott for the WBC and WBA middleweight belts in the early hours of Sunday morning.

Price, who is a unified welterweight champion, has welcomed a future clash between two Olympic gold medallists but Salita believes Shields should receive home advantage for the middleweight fight.

"Claressa came down to middleweight to make the biggest fights possible," Salita told Sky Sports.

"She flew to see Lauren Price fight and I invited Price to be ringside for Claressa's fight on Saturday night.

"We want to make this a mega-event, and I believe that fight belongs in the United States.

"That being said, we love the UK and another fight there is certainly not out of the question. It's an incredible time for women's boxing."

But Shields must firstly overcome Scott in Atlanta to become a middleweight world champion for a third time.

"Scott is ready and highly motivated, and Claressa always comes to make a statement," said Salita.

"I expect an electric fight at State Farm Arena. It will be the first time a woman has headlined a combat sports event in this historic building, and we expect a multi-figure gate.

"That's a tremendous milestone for Claressa, women's boxing and the sport as a whole."

Shields has proclaimed herself as the GWOAT, meaning the Greatest Woman Of All Time, and she can strengthen her claim as the world's no 1 female fighter, with Katie Taylor set to retire next month.

"Every one of Claressa's fights is historic," said Salita.

"This will be only the second time in more than 120 years of boxing that a fighter has come down from heavyweight to become middleweight world champion.

"Claressa is a generational talent and a legacy-defining champion, and August 15 will be another history-making night."

articles.title: ONE Championship: Nico Carrillo knocks out Zhou Jiaqiang in kickboxing debut on ONE Fight Night 46
articles.summary: Nico Carrillo knocks out Chinese star Zhou Jiaqiang in the second round of their featherweight tussle at Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium, proving that his Muay Thai skills brilliantly translated to the kickboxing
articles.body:
The newly crowned ONE featherweight Muay Thai world champion answered questions over how his renowned knockout power would translate from four-ounce gloves to the kickboxing ranks by overwhelming Zhou at Lumpinee Stadium on Saturday morning.

Carrillo had to weather a bright start from the Chinese striker, who enjoyed success with sharp combinations and slick movement during the opening round.

But the Scot shifted through the gears in the second after being caught with a front kick to the face.

Responding instantly, Carrillo unleashed a barrage of punches and forced Zhou onto the back foot as the contest turned into a firefight.

The 27-year-old gradually broke down his opponent with heavy shots to the head and body, a series of left hooks to the midsection proving particularly damaging.

With Zhou trapped in the corner and running on empty, Carrillo closed the show with another sustained assault.

The Chinese fighter eventually fell to the canvas and was unable to beat the count, prompting the referee to wave off the contest at 2:47 of the second round.

The victory was the 30th of Carrillo's professional career and an ideal start to his pursuit of world titles in two sports.

articles.title: UFC 330: Makhachev secures record-setting win against Machado Garry
articles.summary: Islam Makhachev records 17th UFC victory in a row in his welterweight title defeat of Ian Machado Garry.
articles.body:
Islam Makhachev (29-1 MMA) has successfully defended his UFC welterweight championship, defeating ‌Ireland’s Ian Machado Garry (17-2 MMA) via unanimous decision (49-46, 49-46, 48-47) while also setting an impressive record in the main event of UFC 330 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

With ⁠the victory on Saturday night, Russia’s Makhachev etched his ⁠name in the UFC record books, extending his winning streak to 17 consecutive fights and surpassing UFC Hall of Famer Anderson Silva’s historic 16-fight mark set from 2006 to 2013.

list 1 of 4 Swimming: Pallister stuns Ledecky in Pan Pacs, Douglass sets world record

list 2 of 4 MLS: Lionel Messi misses penalty again as Nashville thrash Inter Miami 4-1

list 3 of 4 Bangladesh make history with first-ever Test cricket win in Australia

list 4 of 4 La Liga: The key talking points for Real Madrid before the 2026-27 season

Makhachev dictated the tempo throughout the 25-minute championship tilt, neutralising the challenger with suffocating top control ⁠and chain wrestling while mixing in dynamic striking, including a damaging second-round head kick.

Machado Garry, bidding to become only the second undisputed UFC champion hailing from Ireland, stayed diligent in defensive scrambles on the mat to survive danger but could not mount enough offence to sway the judges’ scorecards.

“I have nothing but respect for Islam. … He ⁠won. I have no complaints, no excuses,” Machado Garry said inside the Octagon after the decision.

“It’s always hard,” Makhachev said of grinding out the victory against the challenger in the championship rounds.

In the co-main event, UFC women’s strawweight champion Mackenzie Dern (17-5 MMA) successfully defended her title for the first time, using dominant grappling and relentless submission threats to defeat Canada’s Gillian Robertson (17-9 MMA) via unanimous decision (49-46, 49-46, 48-47).

Dern, a Phoenix native who fights out of Southern California, controlled the pace on the mat across 25 minutes, constantly threatening ‌transitions and clinching attacks against her fellow Brazilian jiujitsu standout. Dern’s most dangerous moment came in the opening frame, nearly securing a buzzer-beating rear-naked choke just before the horn sounded.

While Dern had voiced confidence throughout fight week that she would finish Robertson inside the distance, the champion was pleased with her complete five-round performance.

“She’s good. … Thank you, [everyone]). I appreciate you,” Dern said inside the Octagon after her win.

The UFC heads to the West Coast next Saturday, returning to Sacramento, California, with a five-round middleweight nontitle UFC Fight Night headliner pitting Anthony Hernandez, who fights out of nearby El Dorado Hills, California, against Gregory Rodrigues of Brazil. The main event will conclude a 13-fight slate.

articles.title: Claressa Shields stops Kaye Scott to reclaim WBC and WBA middleweight belts
articles.summary: Claressa Shields reclaimed the WBC and WBA middleweight titles with a sixth-round stoppage of Kaye Scott in Atlanta and is now expected to face Britain’s Lauren Price; Shields' promoter believes the Welsh fighter should travel to the US for the potential showdown
articles.body:
Shields had moved down from heavyweight to middleweight for the bout and in the process, became a middleweight world champion for a third time.

The fight was under Shields' control throughout, with the crucial moments coming in the sixth round when the 42-year-old Scott was dropped before being subjected to a barrage of punches against the ropes.

The onslaught continued, prompting Scott's corner to throw multiple towels into the ring, bringing an end to the contest after one minute and 38 seconds of the sixth round.

With the victory, Shields improves to 19-0, further strengthening the self-proclaimed GWOAT - meaning Greatest Woman of All Time - and her claim to being the world's No 1 female fighter, particularly with Katie Taylor set to retire.

"It was a hard camp," Shields said. "I always tell myself that everything is easy work, but it was a really hard camp.

"I cut 38 pounds. I started 14 weeks ago at 198 and got down to 160. It was the most disciplined I've been since the Olympics, I feel like.

"She was stronger than I thought. She was very strong. I knew that, with the amount of weight I'd cut, I didn't want to exert too much energy early.

"I was trying to make sure I could deal with her strength and not get caught with anything crazy, because I'm not as strong as I feel at 175."

Lauren Price is now Shields' preferred opponent at 160lbs, with the American saying she wants the fight to take place between December and January.

It is a fight that Price has welcomed, but the American star's promoter, Dmitriy Salita, believes the "mega" event "belongs in the United States".

"Claressa came down to middleweight to make the biggest fights possible," Salita told Sky Sports .

"We want to make this a mega-event, and I believe that fight belongs in the United States.

"That being said, we love the UK, and another fight there is certainly not out of the question. It's an incredible time for women's boxing."

articles.title: Claressa Shields vs Lauren Price talks are 'ongoing' after American star reclaimed world middleweight titles in Atlanta
articles.summary: Claressa Shields became world middleweight champion for a third time after a sixth-round stoppage of Kaye Scott in Atlanta; promoter Dmitriy Salita says talks are 'ongoing' for Shields to face Lauren Price who is a unified world welterweight champion and a fellow Olympic gold medallist
articles.body:
Shields took back WBC and WBA belts with a ruthless sixth-round stoppage of Kaye Scott as the unbeaten Michigan fighter became a middleweight world champion for a third time.

Price, the unified welterweight champion, could be the next opponent for Shields and the American's promoter Dmitriy Salita is keen to finalise terms for a battle between two Olympic gold medallists.

"We're working on it as we speak," Salita told Sky Sports .

"Our intention is to make the fight. Based on my understanding, we have agreed to all the requests from [Price's promotional team] BOXXER and Lauren's side.

"I invited Lauren and her team to the fight because my relationship with the fighters we promote, and certainly with Claressa, is that they know all the moving parts and are business partners in making these decisions.

"I wanted Lauren and Claressa to have an opportunity to sit down together and see if there was anything outstanding. Claressa is extremely intelligent and very experienced in making big fights, and I'm sure Lauren is sharp as well.

"Unfortunately, they weren't able to make it, but the conversations are ongoing and we want to make the fight."

Shields has also been linked with a fight against WBO and IBF world middleweight champion Tamm Thibeault and fellow American Mikaela Mayer, who faces Chantelle Cameron in a unified world super-welterweight title fight in Birmingham on August 29, live on Sky Sports.

"Claressa wants to fight the best and be part of the biggest, most impactful events - that's always been clear," said Salita.

"There are a few other conversations taking place in case the Lauren Price fight doesn't come together.

"We'll make a decision soon, but whatever is next, the goal is for it to be another legacy-making moment for Claressa and for boxing."

Shields attracted a huge crowd to State Farm Arena in Atlanta, including some of the biggest names in boxing and music, and Salita believes his fighter's reputation has transcended sport.

"It was incredible. We were getting calls and requests from some of the biggest stars in hip-hop, music, boxing and culture right up until the final bell," he said.

"Usher, Floyd Mayweather, Kevin Gates, Terence Crawford - and the list goes on. The atmosphere was electric.

"It was a special night in a packed arena and a real reflection of Claressa's star power and how far her reach has grown beyond boxing."
